finding.summary: Data-model semantics change (a `list-item` now carries `headingLevel`) is not recorded in any design doc
finding.evidence: CONTRIBUTING.md:57-61 — “**Architecture / data-model changes** belong in `docs/design/<area>/<topic>.md` … Update the existing doc when evolving an area”. This PR redefines an invariant of the `Block` model (previously `headingLevel` implied `type === 'heading'`; now a `list-item` legally carries an inert level that survives round-trip through the Yorkie tree attrs and the backend `docs-tree` serializer). The only prose is a TSDoc comment on `Block.headingLevel` (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:54-61) and a task todo/lessons pair under docs/tasks/active/. `docs/design/docs/docs.md` is the canonical block-model doc (‘Design decisions → Block type’, line 113-116; ‘Empty list-item Backspace exits the list’, line 135-146) and is untouched, so the doc now describes a model rule the code no longer holds. If the maintainers treat #783 as a plain bug fix, CONTRIBUTING.md:11-12 lets it skip a design doc — hence medium confidence, not high.

verdict.reason: The finding claims the `list-item` + `headingLevel` data-model semantics change is recorded in no design doc, and that `docs/design/docs/docs.md` is untouched. That is false in this working tree. `docs/design/docs/docs.md:117-134` contains a dedicated Design-decisions bullet, "**`headingLevel` on a `list-item`**", stating verbatim that "`headingLevel` no longer implies `type === 'heading'`", giving the Google Docs / Word parity rationale, the inertness rule ("every reader ... gates on `type === 'heading'`"), the explicit statement that the level "round-trips through the Yorkie tree node attributes and the backend `docs-tree` serializer" (the exact persistence detail the finding says has no prose), and the writer contract through `unlistedBlockType(block)` across the three `toggleList` implementations. It sits directly after the `Block type` bullet the finding cites (113-116), i.e. folded into the canonical subsystem doc rather than a parallel file, satisfying CONTRIBUTING.md:57-61. The adjacent "Empty list-item Backspace exits the list" section was also updated to cross-reference it (docs.md:166-170). The doc matches shipped code, not a stale rule: packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:54-62 carries the corresponding TSDoc and types.ts:337-344 implements `unlistedBlockType` returning the remembered heading level. The doc is properly indexed at docs/design/README.md:38. The reviewer's reported empty grep for `headingLevel` in docs/design does not reproduce — it returns docs.md:117 and docs.md:170. Whether the diff introduced these lines is decided separately per instructions; the design-doc discipline requirement is met.

finding.summary: Only `toggleList` exits through `unlistedBlockType`; the other two list-exit gestures still hardcode `'paragraph'`, so the same user intent gives two different results
finding.evidence: `Doc.splitBlock` (document.ts:297-301, Enter on an empty list item — “exit list by converting to paragraph”) and `Doc.deleteBackward` (document.ts:262-266, Backspace at offset 0 of an empty list item — documented in docs/design/docs/docs.md:135-146) both call `this.setBlockType(id, 'paragraph')` unchanged. Those are ‘remove the list’ paths just like the toolbar toggle, so a bulleted Heading 2 emptied and Enter/Backspace-ed out of the list still silently becomes body text — the exact failure #783 describes, via a different gesture. The todo (docs/tasks/active/20260816-docs-unlist-restores-heading-todo.md:46-52) lists ‘splitting a bulleted heading (Enter)’ as a non-goal, but that non-goal is about the *new* item after a mid-text split, not about the empty-item list-exit branch, so the gap looks unintended and undermines the stated point of the shared helper (‘keeps the three toggleList implementations from drifting’).

verdict.reason: The finding says `Doc.splitBlock` and `Doc.deleteBackward` still hardcode `this.setBlockType(id, 'paragraph')` for the empty-list-item exit, diverging from `toggleList`. The code is not as described. `document.ts:263-270` (deleteBackward) and `document.ts:301-307` (splitBlock) both compute `const exit = unlistedBlockType(block)` and call `this.setBlockType(id, exit.type, exit.opts)`; `unlistedBlockType` is imported at document.ts:28. A repo-wide grep for `setBlockType(...'paragraph')` returns zero hits in document.ts; the only production hits are text-editor.ts:952 (Cmd+Alt+0 "Normal text") and text-editor.ts:1030 (Cmd+Alt+1-6 heading toggle-off), which are the explicit "Normal text" commands the todo at docs/tasks/active/20260816-docs-unlist-restores-heading-todo.md:31-32 deliberately keeps clearing — not list-exit gestures. The design doc (docs/design/docs/docs.md:128,167) already states splitBlock and the Backspace path resolve through `unlistedBlockType()`, consistent with the code. Since all three list-exit gestures already share the helper, the claimed spec gap does not exist.
